headline: Visit Greater Palm Springs manages a $9 billion tourism economy but is functionally invisible to the AI systems mediating high-value buyer decisions in 2026.
buyer_readiness_summary: VGPS manages a $9B tourism economy and 14.5M annual visitors but has not built a strategy for the SF/LA tech-wealth migration segment — the highest-value buyer now evaluating the Coachella Valley.
competitive_summary: Nine-city governance produces a destination narrative that serves everyone and compels no one. Tier-one assets are undersold against Montecito and Napa, which operate with singular, high-conviction positioning.
ai_readiness_summary: Zero schema markup. No API layer. A 15-year-old Simpleview CRM with no structured data export. The official DMO is functionally invisible to AI-mediated luxury travel planning.
confidence: High confidence across all three dimensions — gaps are structural, well-documented, and consistent across council runs.

data_provenance_disclaimer: This review is based on what AI systems, search engines, and digital research tools can currently find and interpret about Visit Greater Palm Springs. We analyze publicly available digital content — website, third-party listings, review platforms, media coverage, and structured data signals. What exists operationally but isn't documented digitally is invisible to AI agents and to this review.
how_this_works: The Chairman is AICV's lead synthesis agent. It receives the independent findings of three council runs — Buyer Readiness, Competitive Positioning, and AI Readiness — each deliberated by a panel of five frontier AI models. The Chairman synthesizes across all fifteen perspectives and delivers a single verdict calibrated for the Coachella Valley's intelligence layer. This is not a consultant's opinion. It is what fifteen AI systems currently understand about your property, filtered through deep regional knowledge.
